record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one analyze the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, in analogy with the analysis of spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar-field equations?

evidence.quote: (iii) analyse the time dependent spherically symmetric equations, analogous to the analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations in [CD2];

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills equations in 3+1 dimensions for a Lorentzian metric $g$ coupled to a connection $A$ on a principal $SU(2)$-bundle, given by
$$ R_{\mu
u} - 	frac{1}{2} R\, g_{\mu
u} = 8\pi T_{\mu
u}[F], \qquad D_\mu F^{\mu
u} = 0,$$
where $F = dA + A\wedge A$ is the Yang–Mills curvature and $T_{\mu
u}[F]$ is the associated stress-energy tensor. Impose spherical symmetry by requiring $SO(3)$ to act by isometries on $(M,g)$ and by gauge transformations on $A$, so that in standard coordinates the gauge potential reduces to a single real function $w(t,r)$ and the metric takes the form
$$ g = -e^{2
u(t,r)} dt^2 + e^{2\lambda(t,r)} dr^2 + r^2 d\Omega^2.$$
Develop a global analysis of the resulting time-dependent system: in particular, formulate and study the Cauchy problem for asymptotically flat data, characterize the possible long-time behavior (dispersion versus gravitational collapse versus convergence to a static soliton or black hole), and determine the structure of singularities, in analogy with the known global analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field system (formation of trapped surfaces, weak cosmic censorship, asymptotic decay).
artifact.status_search_result: A search shows extensive literature on the static spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills system (Bartnik–McKinnon solitons, colored black holes) and partial results on the time-dependent Einstein–Yang–Mills(-Higgs) Cauchy problem in Bondi coordinates, but no global analysis comparable to Christodoulou's program for the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar-field equations (weak cosmic censorship, trapped surface formation, asymptotic decay) has been carried out. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs equations in Bondi coordinates
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes previous results on global solutions for the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs system under spherical symmetry, with characteristic Cauchy problem in Bondi coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for the time-dependent spherically symmetric EYM(H) Cauchy problem but a Christodoulou-style global analysis is not established.

status_evidence.title: Static Spherically Symmetric Solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills Equations
status_evidence.claim: Static case is well-studied, in contrast to the open time-dependent global problem.
